## Headline

The procedure is written and all three notes files now pass the checks with zero banned words and zero long sentences.

- The procedure lives at notes/procedure.md with nine numbered steps.
- Each of notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md now passes check_file.
- The meaning of each note stays the same.

## Background

The request asked for a reusable procedure, then for its application to three notes files in order. The tools available are read_file, write_file, check_file, and list_files [1].

## Relevance

A written procedure lets any later agent repeat the same fix on more files without new instructions.

## Information

The checks ran before and after the edits [1][2][3][4].

- a.md: one banned word, "clearly". It was removed. No long sentences.
- b.md: one sentence of 41 words. It was split into three sentences.
- c.md: one banned word, "very", and one sentence of 35 words. Both were fixed.

All three files returned zero failures on the final run [4].

## End

I recommend that we:

1. Keep notes/procedure.md as the standard checklist. Blocker removed: ad hoc fixes. Test: Given a new notes file, When an agent runs steps 1 to 9, Then check_file reports zero failures. Cynefin: Clear, by deduction from a fixed check output.
2. Run check_file on notes/procedure.md once to confirm it passes its own rules. Blocker removed: unverified procedure text. Test: Given the procedure file, When check_file runs, Then failures equal zero. Cynefin: Clear, by deduction.
3. Apply steps 1 to 9 of the procedure to any future notes file before merging it. Blocker removed: style drift in new notes. Test: Given a candidate file, When the procedure completes, Then check_file reports zero failures. Cynefin: Clear, by deduction.

## Follow-up

References

[1] User request, "Write notes/procedure.md first... fix the banned words and long sentences of one notes file," this conversation. [P]

[2] check_file result on notes/a.md, first run, this session. [P]

[3] write_file results on notes/a.md, notes/b.md, notes/c.md, this session. [P]

[4] check_file results, final run, all three files report zero failures, this session. [P]

arguments.content:
# Procedure: fix one notes file

1. Read the notes file with the read_file tool.
2. Run check_file on the file path.
3. Note the banned words it reports.
4. Note the sentences over 25 words it reports.
5. Replace each banned word with a neutral word or remove it. Keep the meaning.
6. Split each long sentence into two or more short sentences. Keep the meaning.
7. Write the revised text back to the same file with write_file.
8. Run check_file on the file again.
9. If check_file still reports problems, repeat steps 5 to 8. If it reports none, stop.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service fell back to the database for every request. This continued until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message and runs the job. It then writes the result to the store. It marks the message as done. No other worker picks it up again.
